newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes off, talk of central bank sale.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes off, talk of central bank sale.

text.p: Gold prices came under pressure from heavy selling in early European business on Thursday with some dealers saying a central bank could have been behind the business.
"There were rumours that a European central bank was selling, especially during the Tokyo time frame," a dealer said.
He said estimates of the volume sold were around 600,000 ounces, which was followed by heavy selling by the professionals in London.
Gold was fixed at $368.30 per ounce after $370.90 on Wednesday afternoon.
The market found good buying support near $367.50 and responded with a climb to around $370.00 before profit-taking capped the advance.
"We have seen a lot of profit-taking after the bounce yesterday and there was more taken out this morning. Everybody is playing it very short term," a dealer said.
The dealer added that London was probably net short of gold given the amount of selling seen so far.
"We have probably seen our move for the day now. It will probably quieten down until New York opens," he said.
The market was still essentially bearish, dealers said.

Gold came off three-year lows struck on Tuesday when later that day the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 79 points as Wall Street took its profits from a 500-point rise in the average during November.
The fall in the Dow coupled with weakness in the U.S. dollar encouraged some buying of gold, which was in need of a correction after becoming very oversold during its slide to Tuesday's low point.
Steady selling by producers anxious to protect their income in a falling market and persistent rumours that European central banks had sold put the price under pressure.
On Wednesday the Bank of Portugal formally denied it had sold gold from its reserves.
Silver prices moved with gold in early European dealing, finding support at around $4.72 before moving ahead with the yellow metal to be indicated at $4.75/$4.77, down six cents.
"There was a lot of selling in silver earlier, largely on the back of gold," one dealer said.
Platinum and palladiuim were both relatively quiet.
Platinum was indicated down a dollar at $373.50/$374.50 and palladium was 50 cents easier at $115.75/$116.75.
